common_name: Rosie Posie Hummingbird Mint (Compact Two-Tone Rosy-Pink Agastache)

planting.note: Plant transplants in spring in lean, well-drained to rocky soil in full sun; 'Rosie Posie' is a compact hybrid agastache bred for a tidy, dense, ball-shaped habit and heavy bloom from mid-June through September.

directions: Plant in lean, rocky to gritty, very well-drained soil in full sun; 'Rosie Posie' forms compact, densely branched clumps smothered in spikes of two-tone rosy-pink and magenta flowers from mid-June into September, making it one of the showiest and most uniform of the compact hummingbird mints. Its aromatic, minty-scented foliage is naturally deer- and rabbit-resistant, while the nectar-rich flowers draw hummingbirds and butterflies throughout the season. Thin, rocky or gravel-amended soil improves winter survival far more than fertile garden loam, which tends to shorten the plant's lifespan. Avoid winter wet and heavy mulch piled against the crown.

common_name: Royal Raspberry Anise Hyssop (Meant to Bee Series Hummingbird Mint)

planting.note: Plant transplants in spring in well-drained, gravel-amended soil in full sun; 'Royal Raspberry' is a Proven Winners Meant to Bee series introduction bred for fragrant rosy-purple flowers held in long-lasting burgundy calyxes.

directions: Plant in full sun (6+ hours) in well-drained soil, amending with gravel or coarse sand where drainage is marginal; 'Royal Raspberry' produces abundant fragrant, rosy-purple flower spikes held in burgundy calyxes that retain color and garden interest even after individual blooms fade, extending the display into fall. It is drought-tolerant once established, naturally deer-resistant, and strongly attractive to bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds. Good winter drainage is essential, since wet soil over winter is the most common cause of decline.

common_name: Queen Nectarine Anise Hyssop (Meant to Bee Series Hummingbird Mint)

planting.note: Plant transplants in spring in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; 'Queen Nectarine' is a Proven Winners Meant to Bee series introduction bred for soft peach flowers set off by mauve calyxes.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, average to light soil; heavy clay or constantly wet conditions will quickly kill this agastache, so amend poorly drained sites with grit or raise the planting bed. 'Queen Nectarine' bears soft peach flowers on mauve calyxes from summer through fall, making it a standout color break among hybrid hummingbird mints, and is strongly attractive to hummingbirds, bees, and butterflies. Excellent for rock gardens and containers as well as mixed borders; drought-tolerant once established.

common_name: Flame Purple Garden Phlox (Dwarf Mildew-Resistant Container Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; 'Barfourteen' (Flame Purple) is a dwarf member of the Dutch-bred Flame series, selected for a compact, bushy habit well suited to containers and small-space borders.

directions: Plant in fertile, evenly moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, spacing plants generously to promote airflow and reduce powdery mildew. 'Barfourteen' is a compact, dwarf garden phlox from the Flame series bred in the Netherlands, bearing fragrant, tubular purple flowers with a small darker purple eye in dense, rounded clusters from midsummer into early fall. Its low, bushy habit makes it well suited to container culture, courtyard plantings, and the front to middle of the perennial border. Deadhead spent flower heads to extend bloom, and divide congested clumps every few years in early spring to maintain vigor.

common_name: Flame Pink Garden Phlox (Dwarf Mildew-Resistant Container Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; 'Bartwelve' (Flame Pink) is a dwarf member of the Dutch-bred Flame series, selected for a compact habit and large, fuchsia-pink flower clusters.

directions: Plant in fertile, evenly moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, spacing plants generously to promote airflow and reduce powdery mildew. 'Bartwelve' is a compact, dwarf garden phlox from the Flame series bred in the Netherlands, producing large clusters of fragrant fuchsia-pink flowers with a darker pink eye from midsummer into early fall. Its dwarf, bushy form makes it an eye-catching choice for containers and the front of the perennial border. Deadhead spent flower heads to extend bloom, and divide congested clumps every few years in early spring to maintain vigor.

common_name: Opening Act Pink-a-Dot Garden Phlox (Early-Blooming Spreading Hybrid Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; this Walters Gardens introduction blooms several weeks earlier than typical tall garden phlox and spreads gradually via a slowly stoloniferous habit.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; 'Opening Act Pink-a-Dot' bears near-white flowers marked with a dark pink central star pattern, giving an overall light-pink effect, on a glossy, disease- and mildew-resistant plant that begins blooming earlier in the season than standard tall garden phlox. Shearing spent flowers back promotes rebloom into early fall. The slowly spreading, stoloniferous habit fills in gradually over the years without becoming invasive, making it useful for naturalized drifts as well as formal borders.

common_name: Opening Act White Garden Phlox (Early-Blooming Spreading Hybrid Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; this Walters Gardens introduction is the white-flowered, early-blooming member of the Opening Act series.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; 'Opening Act White' produces clean, pure white flower clusters on a compact, glossy-leaved plant with good mildew resistance, blooming several weeks earlier than standard tall garden phlox cultivars. Shear spent flower heads back to encourage a second flush later in the season. Its slowly spreading, stoloniferous habit fills in over time, making it useful for mass plantings as well as mixed borders.

common_name: Opening Act Romance Garden Phlox (Early-Blooming Spreading Hybrid Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; this Walters Gardens introduction is a pink-flowered, early-blooming member of the Opening Act series.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; 'Opening Act Romance' bears fragrant pink flower clusters on a compact, disease-resistant plant that begins blooming earlier than standard tall garden phlox, extending the overall phlox season in the border. Shear spent flower heads back to encourage continued bloom into early fall. The slowly spreading, stoloniferous habit fills in gradually over the years without becoming invasive.

common_name: Opening Act Ultrapink Garden Phlox (Early-Blooming Spreading Hybrid Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; this Walters Gardens introduction is the vividly deep-pink-flowered member of the Opening Act series.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; 'Opening Act Ultrapink' bears vivid, saturated pink flower clusters on a compact, glossy-leaved, disease-resistant plant that blooms earlier in the season than standard tall garden phlox cultivars. Shear spent flower heads back to promote rebloom later in the season. The slowly spreading, stoloniferous habit fills in gradually over time, useful for both mass plantings and mixed borders.
